final.title: Table extraction starts with one workflow, not a slogan
final.body:
If you are rethinking table extraction, do not start with the tool. Start with one bounded workflow: which document are you handling, what table lives in it, and what happens after someone copies it out by hand? For a small business, that is usually invoice rows, order summaries, expense lines, or a lead spreadsheet, not a grand AI project.

The useful threshold is simple. AI table extraction fits best when the source is digital and consistent: exported PDFs, emails, or files with stable structure and little variation. It is a poor fit for scan-heavy, handwritten, or constantly changing documents. Bareni currently declines scan-heavy, OCR-dependent work, so that boundary matters. No amount of wishful thinking makes a blurry scan behave like a tidy export.

The control pattern should stay human-led: AI extracts, a person validates, and the result lands in your own system. That matters especially where money movement or other high-risk decisions are involved; those still need human approval.

One practical next step is to ask: how many hours a week does this re-entry take, and does it come from the same source each time? If the answer is “same source, repeated work, clear table,” you have a bounded workflow worth diagnosing. If not, you may need a different process before you need automation.
